title: Audit Windows owner death at the shared gate and event-open boundary
body:
An unassigned Windows gate can outlive an abruptly terminated owner after it has opened its event. The retained gate waits for its original 30-second timeout without starting the requested workload. If the owner dies before that open, the real `OpenEventW` instead fails and the gate exits; after successful Job Object assignment, owner death stops the gate and ready descendants.

This supplies the source-pinned native audit requested by [#4905's handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19134563). It directly exercises current main's shared `run_windows_command` and the frozen opt-in stream owner from #5463. **The production implementation and selected frontier are unchanged.**

[Audit, reproduction and limits](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/682687b4b41d3252ca6ea1a50e62aee83cf56ca2/docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/README.md) · [canonical claim/result](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472#discussioncomment-19174060)

The contribution centers on the shared-runner handoff, the two sides of the event-open race, and a kill-on-close-disabled counterfactual. The submission refresh exposed [a concurrent stream-adapter audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4681#discussioncomment-19174028); its overlapping three stream cuts are credited as independent corroboration. [Scope coordination](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4681#discussioncomment-19174200). These are separate Codex-assisted sessions under the same account, not independent human review.

Validation at `682687b4b41d3252ca6ea1a50e62aee83cf56ca2`, native Windows 11 build 26300 / CPython 3.12.0 x64:

- **14 cases pass in each normal and optimized mode:** before event opening, waiting before assignment, assigned before release, ready workload/child after release, normal resume, and two actual weakened controls, for both targets.
- Bypassing the gate is rejected for starting work before assignment. Disabling kill-on-close is rejected for leaving the gate/workload/child alive after owner termination.
- Native handles identify the live processes before termination. Observations precede the separate outer fixture job's cleanup; every fixture is subsequently stopped.
- The optimized complete run succeeds in a standalone copy with no `.git` and empty `PATH`. A changed executable source byte rejects before fixture launch or receipt creation.
- Exact source commit/blob/SHA256 bindings, original versus mutant gate hashes, receipt coverage, staged bytes and `git diff --check` pass. Raw native receipts retain their bytes.

[Normal receipt](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/682687b4b41d3252ca6ea1a50e62aee83cf56ca2/docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/evidence/windows-normal.json) · [optimized receipt](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/682687b4b41d3252ca6ea1a50e62aee83cf56ca2/docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/evidence/windows-optimized-standalone.json) · [source and overlap validation](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/682687b4b41d3252ca6ea1a50e62aee83cf56ca2/docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/VALIDATION.json)

```text
python -I -W error -B docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/probe.py --output normal.json
python -I -O -W error -B docs/research/windows-owner-death-audit/probe.py --output optimized.json
```

The original gate algorithm executes with explicit native-call tracing and controlled pauses; this is instrumented evidence, not a natural-crash frequency or universal crash-safety claim. All cases use nested fixture jobs. Other Windows/Python versions, restrictive job policies, death inside native API calls, complete consumer integration and hosted native CI are untested. The transient unassigned waiter is observed, not repaired. This native-only audit is not registered as a generic Linux research replay. The selected baseline attempt stopped at a sparse-omitted certificate; no baseline pass, selected cold replay or mathematical acceptance is claimed.

Started from and refreshed against canonical main `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`, priority revision 7. Final overlap covered 379 open PRs, 4,797 Discussion records and all 7,402 tracked in-scope notes, with reported complete pagination/inventory, followed by direct live claim checks. Coverage is not a novelty guarantee.

Credit ywz65 (#2469/#2452), Mihir Srivastava (#4683/#4905/#5463), Nick Petalas, Brian/JoyboyBrian, Paul Romeo, Douglas Colkitt, Aaron Wang/navinor, woklerx, Tekalign, Arham Tahir and the retained source/lifetime lineage. Prepared for Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, one agent; Apache-2.0. Original source headers and notices are retained.
